name: Right-Wing Accelerationism
summary: Right-wing accelerationism holds that capitalism and technology are a self-reinforcing process that should be pushed faster, and that democratic and egalitarian politics act as brakes on it. In Nick Land's version, developed with neoreactionary thinkers such as Curtis Yarvin, this leads to rejecting democracy in favour of CEO-run or monarchical city-states that citizens can leave ('no voice, free exit'), together with hostility to egalitarianism, welfare and the 'Cathedral' of media and academia, and openness to hereditarian ideas about race.
scope: The profile represents Nick Land's post-CCRU 'Dark Enlightenment' strand of accelerationism and its neoreactionary milieu (Land, with Curtis Yarvin's neocameralism and exit ideas), as set out in Land's 2012 essay series and described in Wikipedia's articles on accelerationism, the Dark Enlightenment and Land. It excludes the violent white-nationalist 'terrorist accelerationism' of groups using collapse to force an ethnostate, and the left accelerationism of Srnicek and Williams. Land's own writing is silent on many everyday policy questions, so many answers are low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Nick Land
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who developed accelerationism and later became a foundational thinker of the Dark Enlightenment.

keyFigures.name: Curtis Yarvin
keyFigures.role: Neoreactionary writer (Mencius Moldbug) whose neocameralism and 'Cathedral' concepts Land adopted, named as a right accelerationist.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Land attacks the "cancerous entitlement state" and welfare dependency as the democratic capture of economic product, so a state-guaranteed health system is the kind of entitlement he opposes.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors are an egalitarian intervention that democratic rent-seekers impose on markets; the Landian line wants labour priced by capital's competitive circuit.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Land treats capitalism as a self-reinforcing positive feedback circuit and the engine of modernity, and the state as a drag on it, so markets are claimed to outperform governments by their nature.

public-ownership.rationale: The gov-corp model privatises even sovereignty into tradable shares; nationalised utilities would be classed with the democratic state capture Land condemns.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Land describes democratic redistribution as demosclerosis, special interests capturing economic product, so higher taxes on the wealthy are the problem not the cure.

unions-good.rationale: Land lists dead-end labour unions among the constituencies that win electoral majorities and expand the state; adherents see them as brakes on capitalist acceleration.

property-fundamental.rationale: The neocameralist state is a shareholder-owned corporation and exit presupposes secure property, but accelerationists also welcome capital dissolving older arrangements, so agreement is moderate.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is a braking mechanism on technocapital in the accelerationist view; Land wants capitalism's self-propelling dynamics unrestrained.

cut-welfare.rationale: Land's essay describes welfare dependency and the entitlement state as the "broken promise" of mature liberalism and endorses incentive structures that punish the maladapted.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is an egalitarian scheme; the neoreactionary model puts ownership with shareholders and a CEO.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Neoreactionaries favour a strong, secure state under a CEO but also libertarian-leaning exit, and sources give no clear position on counterterror surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Land's texts stress personal and economic freedom under gov-corps like Singapore and Dubai, which police drugs severely; neither answer is documented.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Land devotes a passage to 'hate' as the religious orthodoxy of the Cathedral, an offence against its spiritual guidance, and rejects hate-crime and hate-speech concepts.

strong-leader.rationale: Land and Yarvin propose a CEO-run state, a dictator-president or capitalist monarch who can govern without democratic gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Land wants a minimal, efficient sovereign gov-corp rather than no state; the answer is mixed because he distrusts the democratic state but endorses an authoritative one.

limit-guns.rationale: The essay mentions gun ownership only in passing among rights the left restricts; positions on gun control are not formalised.

empower-police-military.rationale: A secure, clean, well-run gov-corp is the model, but Land never makes police and military funding a theme.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Land does not address sex work; the neoreactionary milieu is indifferent or hostile.

decide-locally.rationale: The Patchwork idea of many small competing jurisdictions under exit means governance at small scale rather than a single national government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Land favours incentive structures that punish the maladapted; rehabilitation as the prison goal is rarely discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Land welcomes capitalism dissolving traditional social forms, while the wider neoreactionary milieu is traditionalist; no clear common line.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Land does not make this a central issue and the milieu divides between libertarian and traditionalist stances.

abortion-legal.rationale: No stated position in Land's work on abortion; adherents differ between libertarian and traditionalist views.

more-religion-public.rationale: Land analyses progressivism as a quasi-religion (Universalism) and is not a religious restorationist, though some neoreactionaries are.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Land rejects the Cathedral's egalitarian race orthodoxy and the notion of corrective programmes, endorsing 'racial realism' and what he calls hyper-racism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Land attacks the Standard Social Scientific Model, the blank-slate doctrine that culture accounts for everything, which makes social-construct claims about gender doctrinally opposed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Land stresses capitalism's dissolving of traditions and has no nationalist cultural program; others in the milieu differ.

gradual-change.rationale: Accelerationism asks for speeding up, not respecting, existing institutions, and Land is a hyperstitional revolutionary of capital rather than a gradualist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Land's tweets on immigrants and Muslims ended his New Centre relationship, but his formal framework is open to exit and mobility.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International bodies are part of the Cathedral-type universalist order; the favoured model is small competing sovereign gov-corps.

free-trade.rationale: Land sees global capitalism as the runaway engine of modernity and Singapore and Hong Kong as models, so open trade is favoured as part of the acceleration.

nation-first.rationale: Land's loyalty is to the technocapital process and to competing jurisdictions, not to national interest, though nationalist neoreactionaries exist.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Land treats universalist human-rights morality as the Cathedral's creed, so military action in its name is rejected.

open-borders.rationale: Exit presupposes freedom to leave, but Land's hyper-racism and tweets on immigrants show no support for borders being open to everyone.

limit-growth.rationale: Land defines modernity as sustained growth beyond population and condemns the socio-political forces that capture and limit it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Drastic state climate programmes are a democratic-progressive brake on technocapital that Land opposes.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Land sees techno-science and capitalism as an integrated self-improving machine, with the singularity as the goal, though he does not frame it as human problem-solving.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not a documented theme, but pro-industrial acceleration favours abundant energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Land describes neoreactionary exit rather than revolution and prefers hyperstition and capital's own dynamics to political revolt; militant strands differ.

experts-over-public.rationale: Land's rejection of the 'howling irrational mob' of democracy in favour of competent CEO governance implies expertise rather than popular opinion decides.

central-planning.rationale: Land holds that acceleration is intrinsic to capitalism and impossible for non-capitalist systems.

socialized-markets.rationale: Land welcomes capitalism proper and sees collective ownership as an egalitarian brake, so it is no acceptable compromise.

land-value-tax.rationale: No documented position among Landian accelerationists.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Heavy inheritance taxes are a redistributive entitlement-state measure, and the gov-corp model rewards long-term owners.

basic-income.rationale: Land opposes the welfare dependency of the entitlement state; accelerationist figures sometimes float basic income, so the answer is weak.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protection restrains capital's global circuits, which accelerationism wants intensified.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Land favours a CEO-run state in a competitive market of states, but is hostile to state direction of the economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land welcomes capitalism's concentrating and disintegrating dynamics, with no commitment to dispersed property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Land calls capitalism the self-reinforcing circuit of money, machines and information; abolishing money abolishes the engine.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Austro-libertarian influences are present in neoreaction, but Land does not take a position on central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages are a collectivist brake on the market.

one-party-rule.rationale: The favoured form is a CEO or monarch, not ideologically guided party; Land admires China's results more than its party ideology.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Yarvin calls himself a royalist and Jacobite, Land praises enlightened absolutism like Frederick the Great, and the sources favour monarchic government.

democracy-best.rationale: Land's essay holds that democracy is not merely doomed but doom itself, a vector toward zombie apocalypse.

direct-votes.rationale: Land treats democratic voice as the problem and advocates 'no voice, free exit'; more popular votes deepen it.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils are a democratic egalitarian structure and opposed to the CEO model.

right-to-secede.rationale: Patchwork and 'free exit' rely on small jurisdictions able to leave larger states, and the Land source praises exit over voice.

natural-rulers.rationale: Land and Yarvin reject egalitarianism and favour rule by competent owners and CEOs, while Land embraces hereditarian arguments.

political-violence-never.rationale: Land does not endorse violence as a program, but militant accelerationists do; the document lists violence under militant strands.

war-builds-character.rationale: No documented stance in Land or Yarvin; militant strands romanticise collapse.

separate-church-state.rationale: Land analyses progressivism as religion but offers no program on church-state separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Land is not a theocrat and describes Christianity as a source of the progressive creed.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Neocameralist gov-corps and Hoppe's private-law society treat security as a service provided for customers.

military-superiority.rationale: Not a stated theme in the sources.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Gamez describes neoreaction seeking an ethno-economy, but Land's own model is exit-based competing jurisdictions rather than ethnostates.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Land treats capital's feedback circuit, not class struggle, as the driver of history, though his early work engaged Marx.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Land rejects egalitarian ideals as a dangerous axiom and attacks substantial-egalitarian policy.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No stated position; collectivist group rights are not part of the individual-owner framework.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are a redistributive progressive measure of the Cathedral kind.

civilizational-union.rationale: The model favours fragmentation into many small gov-corps rather than blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Capitalism's self-interested competition is welcomed as the engine of acceleration, though Land frames this in systemic rather than moral terms.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Land rejects collectivist obligation framing; sources give no direct statement.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Land's technocapital view treats nature as material for manipulation and welcomes anti-humanist machine futures.

limit-population.rationale: Land discusses the Malthusian trap as escaped through growth; birth policy is not a stated program.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Land celebrates the industrial revolution and techno-industrial development as the positive component of modernity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The defining accelerationist claim: push capitalism and technology faster, treating democratic restraints as brakes, with the singularity as the aim.

human-enhancement.rationale: Land's 'Bionic Horizon' essay says to be understood is to be modifiable and biology and medicine co-evolve with techno-science.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Land envisions machine intelligence surpassing humans, but states no specific program for algorithmic governance.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Exit and crypto-libertarian strands are close, but Land has no stated position.

restore-past-order.rationale: Land says there is no need to return to the past and that reaction lies in escaping democracy forward into techno-capital; Yarvin's restoration of monarchy is a minority theme.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The neocameralist case rests on efficiency and customer value, judging governments by quality of service.

direct-action.rationale: Land stresses exit and hyperstition rather than street politics; militant strands differ.

means-match-ends.rationale: No stated position; Land's approach is cynically instrumental.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Land celebrates escape from the Malthusian trap through industrial modernity and techno-science.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Capitalist specialisation and the integrated techno-industrial system are what accelerationism intensifies.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Land denounces egalitarian welfare and rewards contributions to the capital circuit.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for profit is the core self-reinforcing circuit of capitalism for Land.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Land celebrates profit and capital as productive; exploitation theory is rejected, though his early work was Marxist-adjacent.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Land rejects egalitarian dictatorships and favours capitalist monarchism.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivised agriculture is anathema to market-based capitalism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Land treats capitalism as productive and positive, not war-causing; the militant strand sees violence as collapse strategy, not capitalism's result.

taxation-theft.rationale: Gov-corp taxes are framed as sovereign rent paid for service, but Hoppe-style critiques of democratic taxation are within the milieu, so agreement is moderate.

harm-principle.rationale: No clear stance; Land is libertarian in some respects and authoritarian in others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Land mocks natural-rights talk as part of the progressive creed, yet favours individualistic exit.

conscription.rationale: Not a stated theme; the voluntary customer model of gov-corps points against it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Land's essay is built on Voice versus Exit, endorsing 'No Voice, Free Exit' over democratic participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Neocameralism treats the state as a joint-stock corporation run by a CEO for shareholder value with residents as customers who can leave.

positive-liberty.rationale: Land holds liberty as negative liberty and exit, and treats material-entitlement claims as egalitarian creed.

media-academia-power.rationale: The Cathedral, Yarvin's term adopted by Land, is the media-academic complex he calls the dominant ruling entity of democratic polity.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Land draws on HBD writers and proposes 'hyper-racism'; the Dark Enlightenment is described as endorsing human biodiversity claims.

organic-representation.rationale: Not a stated theme; Land prefers CEO rule over any form of representation.

total-state.rationale: Land wants a minimal formalised gov-corp focused on security and efficiency, not a state directing culture and education.

national-rebirth.rationale: Land describes a 'Western Renaissance' as possible but incredible, and not as a project.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not discussed; the favoured model is small competing gov-corps.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Formalised property-based sovereignty is preferred to personal feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Land values free exit and labour mobility as the check on government.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Land attacks the Cathedral's thought suppression as ideology, but defends detached scientific appraisal and naturalism.

universal-morality.rationale: Land sees universalist morality as the Cathedral's religious creed and mocks natural-rights confidence.

single-common-good.rationale: The model is shareholder value and customer choice, not a rationally derived common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in Land's essay; the milieu varies.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Land's essays say nothing on diaspora return rights, and the exit model concerns individual mobility, not national homelands.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist cultural project the Landian texts never take up.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Land denounces democracy in all forms and wants owners and CEOs to govern, as in neocameralism.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market choice in services fits the customer model, and libertarian neoreactionaries favour school choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Land treats entitlement-driven fiscal expansion as demosclerosis, so fiscal restraint is supported.

economic-freedom.rationale: Land accepts that Singapore-type states lack political freedom while delivering economic freedom, so economic freedom is expected without political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: No stated position; the model is efficient administration.

national-self-determination.rationale: Land favours small jurisdictions under exit rather than national self-determination as a principle.

force-without-un.rationale: No stated position on foreign force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Land praises detached scientific appraisal while analysing progressivism as faith; he also proclaims hyperstitional ideas.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Land's tweets on immigrants and Muslims suggest this, but welfare itself is opposed in principle.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Land wants incentives that punish the maladapted, so work requirements fit, though he prefers eliminating welfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: Land's texts do not treat labour-capital relations as a partnership question, so neither answer is documented.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Accelerationism welcomes the dissolving of traditional forms, but cultural institutions are not discussed.

dominated-front.rationale: Land admires China and Singapore but offers no program for a bloc against the West.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Land does not discuss it; traditionalists in the milieu favour it, libertarians do not.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest and credit are part of the capitalist circuit Land celebrates.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Land favours racial realism but exit-based sorting among jurisdictions, not state classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Land sees the democratic state as captured by rent-seeking interests and the Cathedral rather than a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Pro-industrial acceleration suggests agreement, but fuel policy is not stated.

elite-replacement.rationale: The essay discusses immigration and the Cathedral, but does not endorse a replacement conspiracy; the militant strand does.

proportional-representation.rationale: Land rejects democratic mechanisms as a whole.

national-mission.rationale: Land criticises the Universalist missionary impulse of progressive democracy.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Land rejects the Cathedral's constructivist dogma and feminist-style structural claims.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Land holds that democratic politicians are driven to vote-buying and corruption, calling democracy 'comprehensive social corruption'.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Land has written on eugenics and assortative mating, but state coercion is not clearly his program.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No stated position; fits the authoritarian gov-corp model.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Gov-corp concentrates on a secure, clean, efficient country with limited functions, although it is not strictly minimal.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Land has written about elite population divergence by assortative mating, but not discouragement as policy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Land rejects the egalitarian ideal as a universal axiom of the Cathedral religion.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; Land rejects socialism entirely.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Land does not address this; decolonial framing is part of progressive orthodoxy to him.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religion-based personal law is not a topic in Land's essays, and jurisdictional diversity points both ways.

restrict-conversion.rationale: No stated position; liberty of exit points against it.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No stated position; market freedom points against it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Land analyses progressivism as a religion but never addresses religious instruction in state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a stated issue; socialism is rejected.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Land's neocameralism replaces voter consent with the customer's exit, and rejects democratic legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is not a theme; free capital flows are favoured.

population-transfer.rationale: Not a stated program; Land's tweets about Muslims were criticised but no transfer proposal is documented.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Land does not endorse a non-aggression principle and approves of authoritarian sovereigns.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Land states that 'competition is good' and sees competitive capitalism and competing jurisdictions as the engine of advance.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not discussed; Land views the Cathedral's orthodoxy as suppressing dissent, which weighs against it.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Land accepts sovereign authority provided exit exists, and the republican notion of freedom has no place.

separated-powers.rationale: The formalised gov-corp concentrates sovereignty in the owners and CEO rather than checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: Land rejects Leninist organisation; no part of his model relies on revolutionary parties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Land attacks the entitlement state and opposes welfare programmes organised around the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a British policy question absent from the Dark Enlightenment texts.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Land opposes labour unions as brakes on production, but has no stated labour law program.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Land discusses the Malthusian trap but ties escape to growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Land's hyper-racism and HBD-based thinking in the Dark Enlightenment series treat diversity as a source of conflict.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Land rejects democratic selection in favour of competence under CEO governance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: No stated position; sovereign discretion fits the absolutist model, but Land stresses stable formal rules.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are state brakes on market allocation.

party-controls-media.rationale: Land attacks Cathedral control of information as thought suppression, and opposes state control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army is a communist question; Land's CEO-sovereign model is not framed around party command, though he would dislike party rule.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Land's texts do not discuss naturalisation periods.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Land's model pays CEO-level salaries for governance and rejects democratic populism.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not applicable to a model without party politics.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Patchwork ideal fragments sovereignty and exit, opposite of supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Yarvin's dictator-president or monarch commands the state, and the CEO appoints executive officers in neocameralism.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside Land's secular analysis of the Cathedral.

clerical-rule.rationale: Land is secular and anti-theocratic and favours a CEO or capitalist monarch.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: No stated position; Land rejects the left's international solidarity.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Land opposes Cathedral thought-suppression but has no stated policy on artistic censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The CEO-monarch model has no term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a democratic mechanism; no direct statement.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed in the Land essays; Patchwork gov-corps imply no stance on blocs.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Property-based market society rejects abolition of rental markets.

people-in-arms.rationale: No stated position; Land mentions guns only as a political marker.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Land celebrates urban industrial modernity and his Shanghai writing is metropolitan.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is a nationalist theme that Land's fragmentation model does not address.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Land attacks the academic Cathedral, but his framing is of power rather than being out of touch.

death-penalty.rationale: Land's material on Derbyshire and punishment discussions does not set a general position on capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Cathedral-curriculum framing implies opposition to progressive curricula, but no direct statement.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Land criticises creationist Christians and defends evolutionary naturalism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: No stated position; market and exit freedoms point against.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Land discusses race and the Cathedral but not the legal basis of citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: No stated position; state subsidy of culture conflicts with the gov-corp model.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Land does not discuss exemptions from general law for religious minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Land does not take up Mill-style arguments about conformity; his concern is thought suppression by the Cathedral.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt cancellation is a redistributive measure inconsistent with property and capital circuits.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: No stated position; decolonial Marxist framing is rejected.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Land rejects democratic constitution-making in favour of formalised sovereign property.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Land praises Singapore, Hong Kong and Dubai as weak only in political freedom, which he calls unimportant when government is effective.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is an egalitarian transfer the Landian view opposes.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence is not a theme of Land's essays or of the accelerationism articles.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The favoured head is a CEO or monarch not chosen by popular vote.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Land does not discuss central banking, though Austro-libertarian roots would split views.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial bargaining over historic homelands is outside Land's themes.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is held for the owners' value; the common-good limit is not part of this view.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The principle slows technological change, which accelerationism opposes.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual defence treaties are not addressed in Land's essays.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Land does not discuss state control of clergy and church property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The favoured head of state is an executive sovereign, not a symbol.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Free exit and Patchwork support secession and oppose coercing regions to stay.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Patchwork and Hong Kong-style autonomy fit the Landian view of diverse jurisdictions under one wider arrangement.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Land treats religious claims of the Cathedral as myth; a CEO-monarch is not divinised.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Sovereign rent in gov-corps is not a progressive tax, but no flat-tax statement exists.

character-from-environment.rationale: Land assails the blank-slate SSSM and defends hereditarian explanations of human differences.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Land praises absolutism but also stresses formalised, stable rules.

space-expansion.rationale: Techno-futurist accelerationism fits, but space is not a specific theme.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Land rejects mixed rule with democracy; the preference is a unitary sovereign.

leader-cult.rationale: Not a stated theme and ritual honouring is alien to the CEO model.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed in Land's work.

land-redistribution.rationale: Taking estates for redistribution violates property.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not a theme in Land's essays.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Land favours small gov-corps and not irredentism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religious punishment is alien to the exit-and-customer model.

women-must-cover.rationale: No stated position; liberty points against it.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed in Land's essays; competing jurisdictions might favour separate currencies.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The model favours fragmentation not ethnic unification.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cultural autonomy for national minorities is not a theme in Land's essays.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Landian answer is exit, which prefers leaving over fighting for rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Land treats technocapital as the driving agent of history, a materialist view, but he also theorises hyperstition.

ban-cartels.rationale: Land treats concentration as part of capital's dynamics, but antitrust is not discussed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Land stresses markets punishing the maladapted but doesn't discuss bailouts directly.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Land denounces majority rule as democracy's vice and holds that democratic majorities spiral towards corruption.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Land criticises egalitarian quotas as Cathedral orthodoxy and holds that competence should select rulers.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is opposed to global capital circuits.

moral-incentives.rationale: Land holds incentives are the basis of social order and endorses structures punishing the maladapted.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Militant strands endorse it, but Land's mainstream relies on hyperstition and exit.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Monarchism and heritable rule are legitimate in this view.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Land attacks Cathedral control of education but sets no curriculum for national history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Land's hyper-racism and admiration of Frederick the Great suggest sympathy but no direct statement.

patriotic-education.rationale: The CEO model does not rely on civic nationalism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Land rejects racial egalitarian programmes as Cathedral orthodoxy and endorses racial realism.

public-money-creation.rationale: State money creation is a statist alternative to the market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: No stated position; Marxist category rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Land rejects hate and discrimination law as Cathedral orthodoxy and endorses freedom of association.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era treaties are not discussed in Land's essays.

minority-veto.rationale: No stated position, though exit is a form of individual non-consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Land favours sovereign stability, with exit as the only remedy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics does not appear in Land's essays, and his anti-humanism offers no clear implication.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use for food and research is not discussed in Land's work.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Land opposes redistribution as a duty and prefers market incentives.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Land's exit thesis is that libertarians stop paying attention to democracy and opt for voiceless flight.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Land describes the Cathedral's thought control, which pacifies, but doesn't address mass culture itself.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Cathedral concept describes rule by media-academic orthodoxy that secures consent, not force.

native-born-offices.rationale: Land does not discuss limiting offices to native-born citizens.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist claims for lost territory are not part of Land's fragmentation model.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Land attacks the Cathedral orthodoxy and the use of antifascism as its tool.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: No stated position; Land would not defend communism but resists the Cathedral's comparisons.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Land discusses neo-Confederate themes but doesn't state this thesis.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Land does not take a position on monuments and flags.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Land opposes feminism's orthodoxy, but this specific policy is not discussed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Land does not discuss domestic violence services.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Land admires Singapore, Hong Kong and China as non-democratic successes, treating liberal democracy as not universal.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political guardian role for armies is not addressed in Land's texts.

paid-care-work.rationale: Land opposes feminist and entitlement-state claims on the economy.

filial-duty.rationale: No stated position; traditionalists favour it, capitalist dissolution weighs against.

office-by-exam.rationale: The CEO-model rewards competence, and Land admires East Asian technocratic states.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed in Land's essays.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Land treats pay-as-you-go pensions as part of the unsustainable entitlement state, and private accounts follow the market view.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Property is owned by title and shareholding, not communal use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Land rejects parliamentary control over the sovereign.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not addressed in Land's essays.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land favours free capital movement, but nationalist limits are not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Land rejects the Cathedral's equity orthodoxy and endorses hereditarian explanations for group differences.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Land welcomes capitalism's self-propelling commodity circuit.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Foreign insurgency policy is not a theme in Land's essays.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Great-power bloc discipline is a Cold War question absent from Land's texts.

corporate-influence.rationale: Land criticises vote-buying in democracy, but regards corporate governance as the proper model.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Land opposes the Cathedral but does not discuss foreign NGO funding rules.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: No stated position; eugenic strands favour selective natalism.

residents-only-property.rationale: No stated position; market logic opposes it.

job-guarantee.rationale: A guaranteed job is entitlement-state spending and conflicts with market allocation.

democratic-peace.rationale: Land views democracy as the road to collapse and does not take it as pacifying.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Land favours exit over disobedience, and absolutist sovereigns demand obedience.

non-intervention.rationale: Land's essays do not discuss the principle of non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Land criticises unions, so no preference for an industrial form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Cathedral thesis is of an ideological establishment, not an ethnic conspiracy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Land does not discuss the legal status of marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information law is not discussed in Land's essays.

informal-organisation.rationale: Land's exit strategy is individual flight rather than organising informal groups, and he does not address organisational form.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Land criticises universalist order but does not state a rule on constitutional supremacy over international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Land's model rejects ethno-religious state definitions in favour of jurisdictions competing for customers.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary deference to a leading power is not discussed by Land, though he admires China.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Patchwork jurisdictions keep their own taxes and exit, favouring local retention.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Property as a whole is private in Land's view.

defeat-communism.rationale: Land is anti-communist and describes communism as the universal implication of egalitarianism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service-delivery mixes in public systems are not discussed in Land's work.

religion-illusion.rationale: Land analyses the progressive faith as religion but doesn't say religion fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Land calls capitalism a positive feedback circuit and the driver of modernity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Land attacks feminism and rejects transforming the economy for equality.

socialized-care.rationale: State provision of care is entitlement-state spending.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not a theme in Land's essays.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not a theme in Land's essays.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Common-property communities oppose the corporate gov-corp model.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-directed settlement of minority regions is not discussed in Land's essays.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Land holds capitalism is the unique accelerating system and that no third course is needed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing historic land claims are not a topic in Land's essays.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Land does not deny the Holocaust in the essay, although some militant strands do.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: No stated position; libertarian and exit norms point against.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Land condemns Cathedral suppression, so suppression of opposition as policy is rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Land is secular and criticises the Cathedral's heresy-style offences like hate.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Land's tweets about Muslims were controversial, and the doctrine is not part of his framework.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Land is secular and rejects religious legitimacy claims.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Land rejects democratic voice altogether in favour of exit.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Land attacks the Cathedral's constructivist egalitarian orthodoxy and the doctrines of race and gender oppression it propagates.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Land has no stated legal position, though he rejects constructivist orthodoxy.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed in Land's work.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Land reasons within a right-reactionary framework and does not claim to transcend left-right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Land's capitalism is a positive circuit, and his early Marxist-adjacent critique of alienation was abandoned.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Land's 2017 tweets on Muslims cost him an affiliation, but his writing treats this only in passing.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Land treats religious legitimation as a feature of Cathedral progressivism, and sovereignty derives from ownership.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not discussed in Land's work.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Land rejects regulation of private contracts and opposes Cathedral-aligned norms.

social-market-economy.rationale: Land rejects social protection and mixed economy compromises in favour of unrestrained capitalism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: A secure gov-corp state requires force.

rich-first.rationale: Land accepts inequality and holds that competitive growth, with elite divergence, drives development.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc neutrality is not discussed in Land's essays.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Yarvin and Land favour monarchic government with hereditary legitimacy, though CEO succession by appointment is also stated.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Land praises fiscal restraint and opposes entitlement-driven deficits.

property-franchise.rationale: Land favours rule by owners and shareholders, but doesn't specify a franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Land welcomes technological mastery of nature and rejects ecofeminist claims.

reification.rationale: Land's early Marxist-adjacent ideas retain a view of capital as an autonomous system, though he celebrates rather than critiques it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Land claims the Cathedral, the media-academic complex, dominates the press, not the rich, and rejects the critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The formalism strand of neoreaction asks for clear defined property and sovereignty rules, so stable known law is favoured.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Dark Enlightenment endorses HBD but Land's model is exit-based; racial franchise isn't stated.

online-participation.rationale: Land opposes democratic participation in all forms.

open-government-data.rationale: Open government records are not a theme in Land's essays.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: No stated position, libertarian norms point against.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: No stated position; market logic opposes it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Deliberative citizen bodies are a democratic form Land opposes.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Reform of religious doctrine is not discussed in Land's essays.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Land welcomes capital concentration and sees threats to liberty in democracy.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Land does not discuss military service by gay and lesbian people.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Land does not favour state-led worldviews, and criticises Cathedral orthodoxy.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Land wants a secure, clean gov-corp country, and incentives that punish the maladapted.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: No stated position; democratic power sharing is rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Land opposes the welfare state, so private provision is the alternative.

term-limits.rationale: No stated position; CEO model suggests none.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a democratic form Land opposes.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Le's reading says Land embraces human extinction in the singularity.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious office-holding by women is not addressed in Land's essays.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Authority within marriage is not discussed in Land's essays.

rent-control.rationale: Price caps in housing are market interventions Land opposes as the rent-seeking of democracy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed in Land's essays; libertarian opinion differs.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing of nuclear weapons is not discussed in Land's essays.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not discussed in Land's essays.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official genocide recognition is not discussed in Land's essays.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Land celebrates capital and ownership as the engine, rewarding owners.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Land's model rests on force and security; pacifism is alien.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: National continuity myths are not a theme of Land's essays.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Land rejects the Standard Social Scientific Model and defends naturalism about humans.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: No stated position, though Land rejects constructivist orthodoxy.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nationalist martyr cults are not part of Land's techno-commercial framework, though he does not address them.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Land treats progressivism as religion but frames politics as incentives and systems.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora homelands are not a theme in Land's essays.

culture-before-state.rationale: Land's concern is the political structure of exit and sovereignty, not national cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological language is not discussed in Land's essays.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Land welcomes capital competition and has no stated position on ethnic economic control.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Patchwork favours many jurisdictions, no ethnic merger principle.

independent-unions.rationale: No stated position; Land opposes unions.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of utilities is statist.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative design is not discussed since Land rejects legislatures as a whole.

municipal-property.rationale: Community-owned production opposes the corporate model.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Land favours competing jurisdictions, but not municipalist assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Wages should match market value in this view.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Accelerationism favours speeding technological and biomedical change without regulatory brakes.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Land's Bionic Horizon points to biomedical modification, but public funding isn't stated.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Crypto-libertarian affinity exists, but Land states no position.

online-anonymity.rationale: Land's attacks on Cathedral thought-suppression favour pseudonymous speech, but no direct statement.

person-over-state.rationale: Land asserts exit and individual choice but offers a non-humanist technocapital view.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Land's anti-humanist view treats humans as part of a machinic process.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Whether regional powers can be revoked is not addressed; Patchwork favours durable autonomy yet sovereign owners could alter terms.

gm-crops.rationale: Accelerationism favours technology without precautionary restrictions.

dense-cities.rationale: Land celebrates urban modernity, but environmental claims are not discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Land is racial-realist but individualist; the militant strand organises on race.

racial-pride.rationale: Land's essays discuss race realism but not the legitimacy of racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: War aims are not discussed in Land's essays.

language-defines-nation.rationale: No stated position; jurisdictions are not national.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Land does not frame foreign plots to partition countries.

free-public-college.rationale: Land criticises universities as Cathedral and welfare spending.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Land opposes regulatory brakes, but taxes on externalities are not discussed.

future-generations.rationale: Land's anti-humanist view doesn't prize preserving the earth.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Land attacks feminist doctrines and egalitarian orthodoxy.

arms-reduction.rationale: Arms control is not discussed in Land's essays.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret diplomacy is not discussed in Land's essays.

capital-controls.rationale: Land welcomes capital's free global flow and deterritorialisation.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Neocameralism concentrates sovereignty in the gov-corp, but gun rights are mentioned positively in passing by some.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Land does not support left-wing insubordination, preferring command by sovereign.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Individual contracts and market pricing are preferred to union bargaining.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Land attacks demosclerosis and entitlement spending, but no explicit rule is stated.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Land treats the world market as the productive engine.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Land wants a rebuilt sovereign through formalism, but no endorsement of smashing.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Patchwork is competing jurisdictions experimenting with governance and economics.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Land's technocapital view treats all value in commodity terms, but this accounting is not discussed.

sacred-nation.rationale: No stated position; nationalism not central.

internal-colonialism.rationale: No stated position; dependency theory rejected.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Land's anti-humanism treats human nature as something to be surpassed.

public-service-media.rationale: Land views the media as Cathedral and the state media as its apparatus.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Perennialism is not addressed in Land's essays and he treats religions as social formations.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear disarmament is not discussed in Land's essays.

ban-fgm.rationale: FGM is not discussed in Land's essays.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Women's inheritance rights are not discussed in Land's essays.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Linguistic naming disputes are not discussed in Land's essays.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Austro-libertarian influence on neoreaction is noted, but this view is not stated.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary chiefs are not discussed in Land's essays.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Land opposes restricting growth for environmental values.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing law is not discussed in Land's essays.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements are not discussed in Land's essays.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Land opposes unions as brakes and favours market contracts.

voter-id.rationale: Land rejects democracy, so doesn't concern himself with its procedures.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Religious pluralism in law is not discussed in Land's essays.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Land holds democracy is a vector with direction, not merely procedure.

premarital-sex.rationale: Sexual morality is not discussed in Land's essays and the milieu includes libertarian and traditionalist views.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: No stated position; exit and open information favour against it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Land opposes welfare but a negative income tax is a Hayekian alternative; no position.

women-suffrage.rationale: Land rejects universal suffrage as part of democracy, but doesn't isolate the point.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Land treats religion as a social force but does not link it to women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Land defends HBD and racial realism and attacks the claim that race is purely cultural.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Land attacks Cathedral egalitarian institutions and state-run equality programmes.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Austro-libertarian strands matter, but no explicit view stated.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: International courts express universalist Cathedral norms.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Land criticises creationist Christianity and affirms naturalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Gender provisions in Indigenous governance are not discussed in Land's essays.

national-church-status.rationale: Established churches are not discussed in Land's essays.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Patchwork is about small autonomous jurisdictions, but ethnic autonomy is not stated.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Land favours exit rather than votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Postcolonial border policy is not discussed in Land's essays.

simple-living.rationale: Land welcomes capitalism's expansion of consumption and technology.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: No stated position; free movement of capital and persons favours against.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription of women is not discussed in Land's essays.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Land's framework is commercial and does not describe a spiritual bond with territory.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The model stresses formal law, though the document doesn't mention extrajudicial killing.

close-ties-china.rationale: Land praises China, Deng and the East Asian models and lived in Shanghai, favouring them over the US.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Kin-state protection of minorities is not discussed in Land's essays.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Land's property model holds resources owned by title, not commons.

self-ownership.rationale: The libertarian roots of neoreaction support it, but Land is ambivalent about natural rights.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption taxes are not discussed in Land's essays.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The CEO-monarch model bypasses factional interests, though no direct statement.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Land attacks rent-seeking, but the Cathedral concept is more central.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Confessional politics are not discussed in Land's essays.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Land's accelerationism favours technology and capitalism's dissolution of traditional forms over their combination.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Women's divorce rights are not discussed in Land's essays.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource nationalism is not discussed in Land's essays; capital's free flow suggests foreign ownership would be fine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Land does not discuss annexation and the question of consent of populations; the exit framework offers no direct answer.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Land's racial realism and his admiration of Frederick the Great and East Asian states over democratic West treat civilisations as differing in capacity, rejecting relativist equality.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Land welcomes capital's free movement across borders; blocking foreign purchases restrains the circuit.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Land attacks the entitlement state and democratic redistribution, so he treats outcomes of voluntary exchange as legitimate whatever their equality.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not discussed by Land; inferred from his hostility to state interference with capital flows.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Neoreactionary milieu openly entertains hereditarian ideas and rejects egalitarian explanations; inferred from that, not stated for this claim.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Land favours sovereign positive authority over moral law above the state; inferred from his neocameralism.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Accelerationists want technology to displace labour, but Land does not frame it as shorter work for people; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Neocameralism and 'free exit' imagine many competing sovereign city-states rather than one global order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Land treats capital and technology as self-driving processes, not labour-created value; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Land is not nationalist in the conventional sense and rejects the populist framing; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Land is hostile to egalitarian politics of both kinds and has no class-politics program; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Land has admired China's state-run capitalism, but he does not endorse communist party rule as such; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be treated as customers of the state, free to leave for a better-run government, and should have no say in running it.
missingStatements.rationale: Land's 'No voice, free exit' neocameralism makes exit without democratic voice the core political mechanism.

missingStatements.text: Democracy leads by its own logic to ever-greater state spending and social decay.
missingStatements.rationale: Land argues democracy is a vector of corruption, entitlement growth and eventual collapse.

missingStatements.text: Technological and economic progress will eventually produce intelligence that surpasses and replaces humanity, and this should not be resisted.
missingStatements.rationale: Land and commentators describe capital's acceleration toward a singularity that surpasses the human subject.
missingStatements.declined: Idiosyncratic to Landian accelerationism; accelerate-technology and algorithmic-government already place it.

notes: Land himself disputes that neoreaction is a movement and distinguishes the alt-right from it. Militant right accelerationists (Siege-style) would answer very differently on violence and race. Land's early CCRU work was left-leaning and is excluded.
